full_query: How do I know if its a canker sore versus herpes

shared_context.topic: distinguishing canker sores from herpes/cold sores

sentences: Canker sores and cold sores (caused by herpes simplex virus, HSV) are two distinct oral mucosal lesions with different causes and characteristics
Typically appear as small, shallow ulcers with a yellow or white base and a red border
Usually occur on the inside of the mouth, including the cheeks, lips, tongue, and gums
Often accompanied by pain, tenderness, and a burning sensation
Can be triggered by stress, hormonal changes, food sensitivities, or minor mouth injuries
Typically resolve on their own within 1-3 weeks without treatment
Typically appear as small, fluid-filled blisters that eventually rupture and form a crust
Usually occur on the lips, but can also appear on the mouth, nose, or genital area
Often accompanied by tingling, itching, or burning sensations before the blisters appear
Can be triggered by stress, sunlight, or other factors that weaken the immune system
May recur, especially if the virus is not treated or managed properly
To determine whether a lesion is a canker sore or a cold sore, consider the following
Location: Canker sores typically occur inside the mouth, while cold sores usually appear on the lips or other external areas
Appearance: Canker sores have a yellow or white base and a red border, while cold sores are fluid-filled blisters that eventually form a crust
Symptoms: Canker sores are often accompanied by pain and tenderness, while cold sores may be preceded by tingling or itching sensations
If you are unsure about the nature of a lesion or if it persists or worsens, consult a healthcare professional for proper evaluation and guidance
